answer: A potent sybil defense is charging a per-agent stake denominated in compute-hours, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets requires real hardware expenditure rather than a free zephyr of ephemeral identities. Each node posts bond collateral before any reward accrues, making the whole voyage expensive. When peers detect mass identity from one IP cluster, that reef of suspicious nodes triggers stake slashing plus reputation decay, so attackers pay twice, once to build and again to rebuild after forfeiture.
